item.title: What if you didn’t brush your teeth for a year? - Justin Merritt
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Trace the impact that not brushing or flossing can have on your teeth, gums, microbiome, and overall health over time.
--
At any given time, your mouth is maintaining a delicate balance between hundreds of microbial species, which is why dentists agree that you should brush twice and floss once every day. But what if you just… didn’t? If you stopped doing any oral hygiene, how long would it take for your mouth to get messy? Justin Merritt investigates how not brushing can impact your health over time.

item.title: Siemens Mendix SAML Module
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Mendix SAML module contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to gain unauthorized access by replaying a valid SAML assertion in IdP-initiated authentication flows. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.The following versions of Siemens Mendix SAML Module are affected:Mendix SAML (Mendix 10 compatible) vers:intdot/<4.2.4 (CVE-2026-89209)Mendix SAML (Mendix 11 compatible) vers:intdot/<4.2.4 (CVE-2026-89209)Mendix SAML (Mendix 9 compatible) vers:intdot/<3.6.29 (CVE-2026-89209)Mendix SAML (Mendix 10 compatible)Authentication Bypass by Capture-replayCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Information TechnologyCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyAffected versions of the module do not properly protect against SAML assertion replay in IdP-initiated authentication flows. This could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to the application by replaying a valid SAML response.Mendix SAML (Mendix 10 compatible) < V4.2.4Product Status: known_affectedDisable IdP-initiated SSOUpdate to V4.2.4 or later versionMendix SAML (Mendix 11 compatible) < V4.2.4Product Status: known_affectedDisable IdP-initiated SSOUpdate to V4.2.4 or later versionMendix SAML (Mendix 9 compatible) < V3.6.29Product Status: known_affectedDisable IdP-initiated SSOUpdate to V3.6.29 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-137528 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. item.title: Hitachi Energy CoreTec Product
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Hitachi Energy is aware of OS command injection and Dirty Frag vulnerabilities that affect CoreTec product versions listed in this document. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could result in impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation.The following versions of Hitachi Energy CoreTec Product are affected:CoreTec5 vers:CoreTec5/<=3.4.0, 5.0.0 (CVE-2026-13162, CVE-2026-43284)CoreTec4 vers:CoreTec4/<=3.4.0 (CVE-2026-13162)Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'), Write-what-where ConditionCritical Infrastructure Sectors: EnergyCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: SwitzerlandAn OS command vulnerability exists in CoreTec product that allows authenticated users with certain roles to execute arbitrary system commands with full control over the device. The vulnerability exists in the configuration daemon's time synchronization handler, which is responsible for setting the system timezone. When processing timezone configuration updates, the daemon constructs a shell command by concatenating user-supplied input without any sanitization or validation.CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and priorProduct Status: fixed, known_affected, recommendedUpdate to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0CoreTec4 versions 3.4.0 and priorProduct Status: fixed, known_affected, recommendedUpgrade to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0Follow general mitigation factorsA vulnerability exists in the IPsec ESP subsystem (esp4) of the Linux kernel used in CoreTec5 that allows a local unprivileged user to escalate privileges to root. The flaw exists in how the kernel handles memory pages when processing ESP encrypted network packets. An attacker can craft a packet that causes the kernel to decrypt data directly into memory pages it does not own, including cached copies of privileged operating system binaries. When one of those binaries is executed, the attacker's injected code runs with root privileges. In CoreTec5, the vulnerable ESP component is compiled in kernel as a built-in and is present at boot time allowing a local user to exploit it.CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and priorProduct Status: fixed, known_affected, recommendedUpdate to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0CoreTec4 versions 3.4.0 and priorProduct Status: fixed, known_affected, recommendedCoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and priorProduct Status: fixed, known_affected, recommendedUpdate to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0Ritesh Kumar Kalle, Subhojeet Mukherjee, Hishamudeen of the Cybersecurity Research group, Hitachi India R&D Center reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.The information in this document is subject to change without notice and should not be construed as a commitment by Hitachi Energy. For contact information, see https://www.hitachienergy.com/contact-us/ for Hitachi Energy contact-centers.General Mitigation FactorsRecommended security practices and firewall configurations can help protect a process control network from attacks that originate from outside the network. Such practices include that process control systems are physically protected from direct access by unauthorized personnel, have no direct connections to the Internet, and are separated from other networks by means of a firewall system that has a minimal number of ports exposed, and others that have to be evaluated case by case. Process control systems should not be used for Internet surfing, instant messaging, or receiving e-mails. Portable computers and removable storage media should be carefully scanned for viruses before they are connected to a control system. Proper password policies and processes should be followed. Additional information on Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices can be found in the Hitachi Energy “Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices” Cybersecurity Notification. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Hitachi Energy PSIRT 8DBD000258 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. item.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
item.author: Dan Goodin
item.content:encoded: Defenders across the world face the burden of responding to yet another botched code-execution vulnerability, this time in boot-time firmware used by most of the world’s server vendors and data centers.The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II, an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the "preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications." Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft's hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well.The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot, which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install other payloads that also run each time early in the boot process.

item.content:encoded: Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS64: >=10.97|<=10.97.2Product Status: known_affectedMitsubishi Electric ICONICS Suite: >=10.97|<=10.97.2Product Status: known_affectedMitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions GENESIS64: >=10.97|<=10.97.2Product Status: known_affectedMitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions ICONICS Suite: >=10.97|<=10.97.2Product Status: known_affectedMitsubishi Electric GENESIS: <=11.03Product Status: known_affectedMitsubishi Electric is releasing fixed version 11.04 or later for GENESIS. Please download the fixed version from the link below and install it: "https://iconicsinc.my.site.com/community/s/resource-center/product-downloads". For more information on the fixed version, please refer to the Mitsubishi Electric security advisory at "https://www.mitsubishielectric.com/psirt/vulnerability/pdf/2026-006_en.pdf".For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend configuring the PCs with the affected product installed so that only an administrator can log in, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking remote login from untrusted networks and hosts, and from non-administrator users, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. and allowing remote login only to administrator when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend restricting physical access to the PC with the affected product installed and the network to which the PC is connected, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend preventing the user from clicking on web links in emails from untrusted sources, or from opening attachments in untrusted emails, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend installing anti-virus software on the PC with the affected product installed, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend performing the following steps for GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and MC Works64, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. (1) Delete the .dat file at the location specified below. This file name and location is different depending on the product version. (Version 10: C:\Program Files\ICONICS\GENESIS64\Components\ClientChallengeTable.dat; Version 11: C:\ProgramData\ICONICS\11\SecurityChallenges.dat) (2) Create a blank file with the same name and location. (3) Restrict the file system write and delete access to this file to a unique administrator account, different than the GENESIS administrator account.Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS64: <=10.97.3Product Status: known_affectedMitsubishi Electric is releasing fixed version 10.98 or later for GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, and MobileHMI. (Note: GENESIS64, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, and MobileHMI are included in the ICONICS Suite installation.) item.title: Winner, Name that Ware September 2026
item.author: bunnie
item.content:encoded: The Ware for September 2026 is a tire pressure monitor from a late 80’s to early 90’s model Porsche, made by Bosch. According to the submitter:Apparently they were deeply unpopular since the sensor mechanism used transponders fitted into pockets in special wheels, which meant lots of alarms when owners changed to wheels without the transponders. Each wheel’s suspension mounted an antenna operating at a “high frequency” of probably a few MHz. When a tire’s pressure dropped below a threshold, a pressure switch in the transponder would open or close, which would change the signal sent back, and this unit would notice and signal the instrument cluster.Kind of a crazy piece of hardware for the late 80’s – this would be pretty cutting edge for the time. Nobody quite got what the part was – but Drew Macrae noticed the Bosch logo peeking between the pins, which caused me to take a second look at the photo. Good eye, I missed that on my redaction. I’ll give the prize to Drew for calling that one out. I really had to search for it, even when told where it was. Congrats, email me for your prize!

item.title: Эндокринолог №1: Сахар — главный яд XXI века? Доктор Роберт Ластиг
item.content:encoded: В новом выпуске - разговор с Робертом Ластигом, нейроэндокринологом, профессором-эмеритом Калифорнийского университета в Сан-Франциско и одним из самых известных исследователей влияния сахара на обмен веществ. Его лекция «Sugar: The Bitter Truth» набрала десятки миллионов просмотров, а исследования посвящены ожирению, диабету и тому, как современное питание влияет на наше здоровье.Поговорили о том, почему ожирение далеко не всегда связано с перееданием и недостатком силы воли, как сахар влияет на работу митохондрий и почему Ластиг сравнивает фруктозу с алкоголем. Обсудили, сколько сахара можно употреблять без существенного риска для здоровья, чем цельные фрукты отличаются от фруктовых соков и почему даже в привычных продуктах может содержаться неожиданно много добавленного сахара.Также поговорили о пищевой промышленности, ультрапереработанных продуктах, хроническом воспалении и инсулинорезистентности. Роберт объяснил, почему считает инсулин натощак важным показателем метаболического здоровья, можно ли обратить вспять диабет второго типа и почему физические упражнения не всегда компенсируют неправильное питание.▶︎ Соцсети Роберта Ластига:https://robertlustig.com/Threads*: https://www.threads.com/@robertlustig...*Instagram и Threads принадлежат компании Meta, признанной экстремистской организацией и запрещённой в РФ. Социальная сеть X заблокирована на территории РФ.▶︎ Телеграм-канал Глеба Соломина: https://t.me/gleb_solomin▶︎ Мой закрытый телеграм-канал — https://t.me/gleb_solomin/4107▶︎ По вопросам сотрудничества: https://t.me/solomin_pr▶︎ По вопросам сотрудничества (почта): adv@glebsolomin.com

item.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
item.author: Dan Goodin
item.content:encoded: eMudhra, the certificate authority that issued eight intermediate TLS credentials so weak that anyone could mint certificates for any website or mail server—one had a private encryption key of just 4—said it’s getting out of the business.V. Srinivasan, chairman of India-based eMudhra Limited, cited increasing costs and complexities of compliance requirements—paired with the business generating just 1 percent of its revenue. He also said that the emergence of organizations providing TLS certificates free of charge further reduced returns on investment when compared to other products and services the company offers.Don't let the door hit you on the butt“However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” the company continued in a Thursday post. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.”

item.title: 5 sneaky ways stores get you to spend more
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Explore 5 tactics that retailers use to influence what you buy and what you’re willing to pay, and how to avoid being tricked.
--
You’re about to buy some bargain bin headphones when you spot another sale. A different pair that is more expensive, but selling for half their usual price. Which is the better buy? And how do you know you’re not falling for a retailer’s psychological tricks? Explore common tactics that retailers use to influence what you buy and what you’re willing to pay, and how you can avoid being tricked.

item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database, retrieve sensitive administrative credentials, escalate privileges, and perform unauthorized operations such as modifying system configurations or causing a denial of service. Siemens has released a new version for RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW and recommends to update to the latest version.The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW are affected:RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW vers:intdot/<6.0 (CVE-2026-89196, CVE-2026-89197, CVE-2026-89198, CVE-2026-89199, CVE-2026-89200, CVE-2026-89201, CVE-2026-89202, CVE-2026-89203, CVE-2026-89204, CVE-2026-89205, CVE-2026-89206)Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection'), Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key, Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data, Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side SecurityCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in facility names processed during the Bulk Import/Export workflow. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in the Value field of notification conditions processed during the Notification Profile configuration. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize the filename of firmware files uploaded to the system. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly restrict access to sensitive configuration items via specific database queries. This could allow an authenticated attacker to retrieve administrative credentials for various internal systems, leading to unauthorized information disclosure and privilege escalation.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in the Name and Value fields for custom file labels. This could allow an authenticated attacker with administrative privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in device group or facility names processed during the Bulk Export workflow. This could allow an authenticated attacker with minimal privileges to schedule unauthorized operations on devices.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionAffected devices do not properly perform server-side authorization checks for requests to modify the state of scheduled actions. This could allow an authenticated attacker with minimal privileges to retry, stop, or delete scheduled tasks without proper authorization.RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionRUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW < V6.0Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V6.0 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. item.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the additional GNU/Linux subsystem of the firmware version V3.1.7 for the SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP (incl. SIPLUS variant). Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP are affected:SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AB0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AB0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 SIPLUS S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6AG1518-4AX00-4AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AB0)Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion'), Access of Uninitialized Pointer, Active Debug Code, Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value, Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Buffer Underwrite ('Buffer Underflow'), Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition'), Deadlock, Divide By Zero, Expired Pointer Dereference, Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies, Exposure of Sensitive Information in Shared Microarchitectural Structures during Transient Execution, Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow, Improper Following of Specification by Caller, Improper Handling of Invalid Use of Special Elements, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Improper Handling of Missing Special Element, Improper Handling of Structural Elements, Improper Input Validation, Improper Locking, Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character, Improper Null Termination, Improper Privilege Management, Improper Resource Locking, Improper Resource Shutdown or Release, Improper Update of Reference Count, Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input, Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard, Incomplete Cleanup, Incomplete Internal State Distinction, Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size, Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types, Incorrect Privilege Assignment, Incorrect Synchronization, Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast, Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'), Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value, Misinterpretation of Input, Missing Critical Step in Authentication, Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression, Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data, Missing Initialization of Resource, Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime, Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime, Missing Report of Error Condition, Missing Synchronization, Multiple Releases of Same Resource or Handle, NULL Pointer Dereference, Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release, Out-of-bounds Read, Out-of-bounds Write, Plaintext Storage of a Password, Race Condition within a Thread, Reachable Assertion, Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference, Signal Handler Race Condition, Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition, Transmission of Private Resources into a New Sphere ('Resource Leak'), Trust of System Event Data, Unchecked Return Value, Uncontrolled Recursion, Untrusted Pointer Dereference, Use After Free, Use of Externally-Controlled Format String, Use of Uninitialized Resource, Use of Uninitialized Variable, Write-what-where ConditionCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: Germanysshd in OpenSSH 6.2 through 8.x before 8.8, when certain non-default configurations are used, allows privilege escalation because supplemental groups are not initialized as expected. Helper programs for AuthorizedKeysCommand and AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand may run with privileges associated with group memberships of the sshd process, if the configuration specifies running the command as a different user.SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AB0) >= V3.1.7Product Status: known_affectedLimit access to the interactive shell of the additional GNU/Linux subssytem to trusted personnel only.Only build and run applications from trusted sources.Currently no fix is availableSIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AC0) >= V3.1.7Product Status: known_affectedLimit access to the interactive shell of the additional GNU/Linux subssytem to trusted personnel only.Only build and run applications from trusted sources.Currently no fix is availableSIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AB0) >= V3.1.7Product Status: known_affectedLimit access to the interactive shell of the additional GNU/Linux subssytem to trusted personnel only.Only build and run applications from trusted sources.Currently no fix is availableSIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AC0) >= V3.1.7Product Status: known_affectedLimit access to the interactive shell of the additional GNU/Linux subssytem to trusted personnel only.Only build and run applications from trusted sources.Currently no fix is availableSIPLUS S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6AG1518-4AX00-4AC0) >= V3.1.7Product Status: known_affectedLimit access to the interactive shell of the additional GNU/Linux subssytem to trusted personnel only.Only build and run applications from trusted sources.Currently no fix is availableSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the exploitation risk of this vulnerability.Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from the internet.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most recent version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-457936 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. item.title: Siemens SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse contains a Denial-of-Service vulnerability. Improper handling of a network management message could allow an attacker to trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition. Successful exploitation may require the affected network to be re-established to restore normal operation.The following versions of Siemens SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse are affected:SENTRON 3NA COM Fuse vers:intdot/<5.2 (CVE-2024-7322)Improper Verification of Source of a Communication ChannelCritical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyA ZigBee coordinator, router, or end device may change their node ID when an unsolicited encrypted rejoin response is received, this change in node ID causes Denial of Service (DoS). To recover from this DoS, the network must be re-establishedSENTRON 3NA COM Fuse < V5.2Product Status: known_affectedUpdate to V5.2 or later versionSiemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-099819 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices
item.author: CISA
item.content:encoded: Nozomi Networks has published information on vulnerabilities in Nozomi Guardian/CMC. This advisory lists the related Siemens Industrial products affected by these vulnerabilities. Siemens recommends to contact customer support to receive patch and update information.The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices are affected:RUGGEDCOM APE1808 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-33387, CVE-2026-33388, CVE-2026-33389, CVE-2026-33391, CVE-2026-33920)Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine, Incorrect Authorization, Lack of Administrator Control over Security, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and FacilitiesCountries/Areas Deployed: WorldwideCompany Headquarters Location: GermanyA template injection vulnerability was discovered in the Dashboards functionality due to improper validation of an input parameter. An authenticated user with the required privileges can define a dashboard containing a malicious payload, or a victim can be socially engineered into importing a malicious dashboard. When the victim views or imports the dashboard, the payload executes in their browser context, allowing the attacker to modify application data or disrupt application availability.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationAn access control vulnerability was discovered in the Credentials Manager functionality due to insufficient validation of user privileges. A remote authenticated user with limited privileges can view a limited subset of the available entries in the Credentials Manager. The actual credential values are not directly visible, but the user can delete entries or edit their properties. An attacker who deletes or edits an entry can disrupt authentication for dependent devices, and one who manipulates an entry's configuration may be able to indirectly obtain the credentials.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationAn improper certificate/host key validation vulnerability was discovered in the Smart Polling functionality, which established encrypted connections to target devices without validating the remote host's identity, and no option was provided to enable it. A man-in-the-middle attacker positioned between a sensor and a polled device can, during a polling session, impersonate the device and intercept the communication, including the credentials used to access it. The captured credentials can then be replayed to authenticate against the device itself or against other devices sharing the same credentials, allowing the attacker to access and tamper with the device's data and to disrupt its operations.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationAn access control vulnerability was discovered in the Smart Polling configuration functionality due to insufficient validation of user privileges. An authenticated user with limited privileges can remotely bypass the intended access control of the web management interface and modify the Smart Polling discovery configuration. This allows the attacker to disrupt the visibility of assets in the monitored network.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationA cross-site request forgery vulnerability was discovered in the login functionality (both standard and SAML) due to missing validation of the anti-CSRF token. An attacker with a valid account can trick a victim into unknowingly authenticating with the attacker's credentials. Any operation performed by the victim in this state is attributed to the attacker's account, compromising the integrity of the audit trail.RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationRUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMCProduct Status: known_affectedContact customer support to receive patch and update informationSiemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurityFor further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisoriesThe use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.Advisory Conversion DisclaimerThis ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-911336 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. item.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
item.author: Dan Goodin
item.content:encoded: Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday.The hijacking began in late August, when, according to Tor volunteers, the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury, a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago.Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted.
